title: Landing scroll-linked animation runs on the compositor, with no JS animation library
context: On an old iPhone (iOS 27, production build), the walkthrough's main-thread scrub (Motion useScroll/useTransform) lagged visibly behind compositor-threaded scrolling, and GSAP scrub smoothing only masked it. CSS scroll-driven animations stayed smooth. Motion was used only by the landing.
decision: Scroll-linked landing movement (the walkthrough's finger-dot path) uses CSS scroll-driven animations on transform and opacity only, with no per-frame JavaScript. Step state changes discretely: an IntersectionObserver picks the step, and a time-based transition fades the outgoing caption out before the incoming one fades in, so no two steps ever show half-blended. While the walkthrough stage is pinned, the document uses mandatory scroll snap, and one mouse-wheel notch steps once via native smooth scrollTo. Without scroll-driven animation support, or under reduced motion, there is no dot and each rest shows its result. The landing uses no JavaScript animation library: the motion dependency is removed and GSAP is not added.

alternatives.reason: Main-thread scrub lags behind scrolling on an old iPhone.
Smoothing masks the lag rather than removing it, and adds a dependency.

alternatives.option: A crossfade scrubbed by scroll position
alternatives.reason: Captions are half-blended at any off-snap rest.

consequences: Browsers without scroll-driven animations get no finger dot.
Snap applies only while the walkthrough is pinned.
A future layered 3D hero needing a coordinated multi-part timeline must re-evaluate GSAP.
